summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a locale code.
description: `nonValidLocale(value)` is the same test as `!isValidLocale(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
Exactly two ASCII letters, in either case — `"en"`, `"UK"`. A region or a script subtag, as in `"en-US"`, is rejected: this is the short language code, not a full BCP 47 tag.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a locale code; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonValidLocale("en-US"); // => true
nonValidLocale("eng"); // => true
nonValidLocale(""); // => true
nonValidLocale("en"); // => false
nonValidLocale("UK"); // => false
```
